entries.title: Architecture
entries.heading: Architecture
entries.text: Architecture A Python 3.12 modular monolith (FastAPI, pydantic v2, SQLAlchemy 2 on Postgres 16) plus one Next.js app. Package Owns --- --- core typed errors, config, clock, ids, JSON logging with redaction, db, event bus, audit log contracts types generated from contracts/schemas compliance the eleven gates, GateClearance , consent and opt-out, kill switch, complaints telephony dial(clearance) , the only function that places a call campaigns dispatcher, the only caller of dial voice agent, versioned prompts, guardrails, normaliser, tools providers one interface per role, one implementation chosen at boot messaging WhatsApp templates, opt-in and fallback caps handoff , postcall , crm summaries, outcomes, CRM adapters analytics lift against holdout, recovery, resolution time, cost per contact rights , incidents , admin DPDP rights workflow, breach and CERT-In timers, RBAC simulator synthetic callers, line simulator, load and chaos

entries.title: Architecture
entries.heading: Rules that shape the code
entries.text: - One correct path. Exactly one provider per role, chosen by configuration; bad configuration fails at startup with a typed error. No runtime fallback between providers. - Every error derives from AgodaVoiceError and carries a stable code . - Each fact has one owner module. Time is injected, so every timer is testable to the second. - An import-linter contract allows telephony.dial to be imported only by the dispatcher.

entries.title: Architecture
entries.heading: Dial pipeline
entries.text: booking event - holdout - jurisdiction - kill switch - consent - DND - opt-out lock - CLI declared - number series - CLI status - call window - attempt cap and cooldown - GateClearance (single use, 60 s) - dial - agent session - call outcome . The gate decision is written and published whether or not the call is cleared. dial consumes the clearance with a conditional update in the same transaction as the call, and re-checks the kill switch, so a clearance minted just before the switch is engaged cannot dial.

entries.title: Compliance
entries.heading: Compliance
entries.text: Compliance This page is engineering guidance, not legal advice. Indian counsel must sign off on the compliance mapping before go-live; that sign-off is an open discovery item. Each requirement has a test in server/tests/compliance/test .py . A requirement without a passing test blocks the compliance milestone.

entries.title: Compliance
entries.heading: TRAI TCCCPR
entries.text: - Every outbound call is an A2P call; its CLI must be declared on DLT, otherwise CliNotDeclaredError . - Service and transactional calls use only the configured 1600/1601 series; promotional calls (J7, not in the pilot) only 140. A mismatch raises NumberSeriesMismatchError . Which series applies to the client's sender category is to be confirmed. - Every call needs a live consent basis: the transaction relationship, or explicit consent valid for seven days or until revoked. - The preference registry is checked before every attempt. As house policy any DND flag blocks J2; J1 may dial a DND number on a transaction basis only once counsel's sign-off reference is configured. - "Call mat karo" ends the call, marks the number and locks consent re-requests for 90 days. - Any complaint pauses that CLI; two unique complaints in ten days pause all campaigns and page a human. - Dialling only 09:00 to 21:00 recipient local time, configurable narrower, never wider. At most two attempts per event, a 24 h cooldown per number, one WhatsApp fallback per event. The pilot dials +91 only.

entries.title: Compliance
entries.heading: DPDP Act 2023 and Rules 2025
entries.text: Notice in the first utterance and an itemised notice by link; purpose-tagged fields; withdrawal in one sentence or one WhatsApp reply; a child on the line ends the booking discussion; rights requests with SLA timers; breach timers with a 72 h Board report; retention by purpose with a nightly purge; India residency by default.

entries.title: Compliance
entries.heading: Other rules
entries.text: - CERT-In: incident report within 6 h of detection, 180-day ICT logs, NTP sync. - AI disclosure in every first utterance and provenance on every recording. - Payments only through an Agoda-hosted link; no UPI collect requests, no card storage. - None of the 13 CCPA dark patterns in any script or template. - WhatsApp utility templates only, and only to opted-in numbers.

entries.title: Console
entries.heading: Console
entries.text: Console /console is role-based; the role comes from the bearer token. Area admin ops auditor read-only --- --- --- --- --- Campaigns yes yes yes yes Live calls, outcomes, handoffs yes yes yes yes Kill switch operate operate no no Audit log yes yes yes no Eval report yes yes yes yes The kill switch requires a reason and a confirmation. Engaging it pauses every campaign, drops queued dials within five seconds and ends live calls politely; the action is written to the audit log with actor and reason. Every call shows its trace id, which also appears in logs and transcripts. The console client has one interface with two implementations, selected at build time by NEXT PUBLIC AV API MODE : http (requires NEXT PUBLIC AV API ) or mock , a deterministic data layer for development and tests. There is no runtime fallback between them. The UI hides actions a role lacks and the client refuses them; the server enforces the same rules.

entries.title: Contracts and API
entries.heading: Contracts and API
entries.text: Contracts and API contracts/schemas/ .json (JSON Schema 2020-12) is the single source of truth. make gen generates pydantic models ( server/app/contracts/generated ) and TypeScript types ( web/src/contracts ); make check fails on drift. Every record carries schema version , tenant id and trace id . Record Purpose --- --- booking event booking state change; every field tagged with the purposes allowed to read it ( x-purposes ) consent record basis (transaction, explicit, inquiry), channel, expiry, revocation; Consent Manager placeholders cli declared calling number: series, purpose, OAP, A2P declaration, status gate decision immutable per-gate results, written before any dial call outcome outcome, tools called (hashed args), handoff, latency, cost in paise, AI provenance handoff summary five-line case summary with 48 h and 30-day SLA fields complaint UCC complaint, including DLT-forwarded app spam reports audit event one privileged action No contract has a card, CVV, UPI PIN or OTP field.

entries.title: Contracts and API
entries.heading: HTTP API
entries.text: Bearer tokens map to roles (admin, ops, auditor, read only). Endpoints: /campaigns , /calls , /consent , /cli , /handoff , /killswitch , /metrics (Prometheus), /simulate , /rights-requests , /incidents . The OpenAPI document lives at contracts/openapi.yaml , and conformance is tested with schemathesis.

entries.title: CRM
entries.heading: CRM
entries.text: CRM One CrmProvider interface with create ticket and add note . Implementations: mock and zendesk (the client's partner helpdesk runs on Zendesk). salesforce and hubspot are valid configuration values that fail at boot until they are built. Every handoff and every logged case creates a ticket whose body is the handoff summary. Tickets carry the trace id and the masked booking reference, never the full booking ID, card data or a raw phone number.

entries.title: Guardrails
entries.heading: Guardrails
entries.text: Guardrails Guardrails run outside the model, before and after every turn, so they hold even when the model misbehaves. - Tool allowlist. get booking summary , send payment link , confirm details , record special request , log case , schedule callback , warm transfer , mark dnc , end call . Anything else raises ToolNotAllowedError . - Payment credentials. A detector on speech-to-text output finds card numbers (Luhn), OTPs and CVVs, including digits spoken as Hindi or English words, and redacts them before the model or storage sees them. The agent interrupts: "Ruk jaiye ji, card ya OTP kabhi phone par mat bataiye." - Handoff triggers. Requests for a human ("insaan se baat", "manager"), disputes, legal, chargeback, fraud, police, consumer court, two turns with anger at or above 0.7, VIP, two failed attempts at a step, medical emergency, death or safety. - Opt-out. "Don't call", "call mat karo", "band karo". - Consent. Only explicit consent counts ("haan", "bhej do"); backchannels such as "hmm" or "achha" are not consent. - Read-back. Amounts and dates are normalised in the customer's language and must equal the booking record: 4,250 INR is read as "chaar hazaar do sau pachaas rupaye". - Dark patterns. A lexicon and regex pass and a rubric judge covering all 13 CCPA patterns run on every utterance and template; any hit fails the build. - Identity. At most the last four characters of a booking ID are spoken; never an email or card detail. The agent never claims to be human.

entries.title: Handoff and CCaaS
entries.heading: Handoff and CCaaS
entries.text: Handoff and CCaaS A warm transfer always carries a summary of at most five lines, shaped like the client's own case summaries: 1. Who: the booker or a third party, and the language. 2. Booking: masked to the last four characters. 3. What the customer wants. 4. What the AI did. 5. Sentiment, policy references and the next best action. The record also carries the queue, the reason and SLA fields that mirror the 48 h acknowledgement and 30-day resolution timelines. Handoffs are published to av.handoffs.v1 for the contact-centre platform to route. If no human is available, the agent says so plainly and schedules a callback. It never pretends a transfer is happening. Disputes always go to a human, because a technically correct answer may not be a fair one.

entries.title: Holdout method
entries.heading: Holdout method
entries.text: Holdout method - The salt is fixed per experiment, so a booking lands in the same bucket in every process and on every retry. - The holdout is the first gate and nothing overrides it. A held-out booking is never called and never sent a fallback message. - Over 1,000 seeded bookings the test suite expects 100 plus or minus 15 held out and zero held-out dials.

entries.title: Holdout method
entries.heading: Lift
entries.text: Lift is the difference in recovery rate (J1: paid by the payment date) between eligible called bookings and held-out bookings, reported with a 95% confidence interval from a two-proportion test. The same report carries recovery rate, case-resolution time, CSAT from a WhatsApp utility survey (to be confirmed) and cost per resolved contact. Containment is reported per persona, but it is not the headline: a call can be contained and still not move a payment.

entries.title: Kafka topics
entries.heading: Kafka topics
entries.text: Kafka topics The event bus speaks the Kafka API: Redpanda locally, the client's Kafka in production. Messages are validated against their contract before publish and keyed by booking id where the record has one. A publish returns only after the broker acknowledges it ( acks=all , idempotent producer), or raises. Topic Record --- --- av.booking-events.v1 booking event av.gate-decisions.v1 gate decision av.call-outcomes.v1 call outcome av.handoffs.v1 handoff summary av.complaints.v1 complaint av.audit.v1 audit event Retention per topic is stated in contracts/kafka-topics.md . Tests use the memory bus, a deterministic test double that production configuration rejects.

entries.title: Agoda Voice
entries.heading: Agoda Voice
entries.text: Agoda Voice Agoda Voice places compliant outbound service calls in Hindi, English and Hinglish for two pilot journeys: - J1 Payment rescue. A booking whose payment failed, or is pending past its threshold, gets a disclosed AI call that asks for consent to send an Agoda-hosted payment link over WhatsApp. No answer: one WhatsApp utility template, only if the customer opted in to WhatsApp. - J2 Booking confirmation. Confirms check-in date and time, guests and special requests, answering only from the booking record. It carries no offers (decision D-001). - J3 Holdout. 10% of eligible bookings are never called, so lift is measured, not assumed. ProsperOps runs it as a managed service first; the same Helm chart then runs on the client's own Kubernetes.

entries.title: Agoda Voice
entries.heading: What it never does
entries.text: - Moves money: no tool can refund, cancel, re-price, issue credit or waive anything. - Takes card numbers, CVV, UPI PIN, OTP or netbanking credentials by voice. - Pretends to be human, or keeps a customer from a human. - Dials without a single-use clearance from the compliance module.

entries.title: Agoda Voice
entries.heading: Phase 2
entries.text: J4 inbound support, J5 supply onboarding, J6 contact intelligence and J7 promotional offers exist as interfaces only and raise NotImplementedError with a ticket reference.

entries.title: Private deployment
entries.heading: Private deployment
entries.text: Private deployment Build, operate, transfer: ProsperOps operates the service first, and the same Helm chart ( deploy/helm/agoda-voice ) then installs on the client's Kubernetes. - No cloud-vendor dependencies in the chart: Postgres, a Kafka-API bus, LiveKit and the application images. - Provider regions are validated at boot against an allowlist; India is the default. Every out-of-India processor is listed in docs/subprocessors.md . - Sizing comes from measured CPU and memory per session in load tests. - Every model and voice has a row in the licence table ( docs/licences.md ). docker-compose in deploy/ runs the same services locally.

entries.title: Providers
entries.heading: Providers
entries.text: Providers One interface per role, and one implementation chosen by environment variable at boot. The default is mock ; production rejects it. Role Variable Options --- --- --- Speech to text AV STT mock, sarvam, elevenlabs, selfhosted (IndicConformer; licence to confirm) Text to speech AV TTS mock, sarvam bulbul, elevenlabs, selfhosted (Indic Parler-TTS or IndicF5; licence to confirm) Model AV LLM mock, openai, anthropic, vllm Telephony AV TELEPHONY mock, plivo, exotel (SIP trunks via LiveKit SIP) WhatsApp AV WHATSAPP mock, meta cloud api CRM AV CRM mock, zendesk, salesforce, hubspot A configured option that is not yet built fails at boot with ProviderNotBuiltError . A provider failure raises ProviderError . Nothing catches it to try another provider: before a dial the call is not placed; during a call the agent apologises and schedules a human callback, and an alert fires. Voices are stock voices licensed for commercial telephony, never a clone of a real person. Hindi verb gender in prompts matches the configured voice ("bol rahi hoon" or "bol raha hoon"). Real-time voice runs on LiveKit Agents 1.8.13 (pinned; 2.0 is in beta), using AgentSession with explicit turn-handling and interruption options and the outbound answering-machine detection helper.

entries.title: Quickstart
entries.heading: Quickstart
entries.text: Quickstart Requirements: Python 3.12 with uv , Node 22, Postgres 16, Docker (for Redpanda and LiveKit in make up ). All providers default to mock : deterministic, seeded test doubles. Production configuration refuses to boot with any mock provider, the memory bus, SQLite or dev tokens.

entries.title: Quickstart
entries.heading: Configuration
entries.text: Every setting is an AV environment variable, nested with , for example AV COMPLIANCE CALL WINDOW END=20:00 . Items still to be confirmed with the client are configuration with safe defaults, never hard-coded truths; see docs/discovery-questions.md .

entries.title: Quickstart
entries.heading: Console
entries.text: The web app talks to the engine through its own server routes. With AV API MODE=mock (the default) they use a mock data layer; set AV API MODE=http and AV API URL to use a running engine. Sign in with dev-ops-token , dev-admin-token , dev-auditor-token or dev-ro-token .

entries.title: Runbooks
entries.heading: Stop all calling now
entries.text: Console: Kill switch, enter a reason, Engage. API: POST /killswitch with {"engaged": true, "reason": "..."} and an admin or ops token. The effect lands within five seconds; confirm that live calls drop to zero.

entries.title: Runbooks
entries.heading: A complaint arrives
entries.text: The CLI pauses automatically. On a second unique complaint within ten days every campaign pauses and a human is paged. Review the calls on that CLI before lifting the pause; lifting it is audit-logged.

entries.title: Runbooks
entries.heading: Security incident
entries.text: The CERT-In timer starts at detection: a report is due within 6 hours. Record detected at in /incidents first.

entries.title: Runbooks
entries.heading: Personal data breach
entries.text: Record detected at . A detailed report to the Data Protection Board is due within 72 hours; affected principals are notified without delay.

entries.title: Runbooks
entries.heading: WhatsApp quality drops to low
entries.text: WhatsApp sending pauses and a human is paged. Review template wording with the dark-pattern suite before resuming.

entries.title: Runbooks
entries.heading: A provider fails
entries.text: Expect a typed error and an alert. Before a dial nothing is placed; mid-call the agent apologises and schedules a human callback. Do not switch providers at runtime: fix or reconfigure, then redeploy.

entries.title: SDK snippets
entries.heading: SDK snippets
entries.text: SDK snippets There is no packaged SDK yet. The API is small, JSON over HTTPS with a bearer token, so a few lines in any language are enough. These snippets use only standard libraries.

entries.title: SDK snippets
entries.heading: Engage the kill switch
entries.text: Needs the ops or admin role. A reason is required and is written to the audit log with your identity.

entries.title: SDK snippets
entries.heading: Types
entries.text: TypeScript types for every record are generated from the JSON Schemas into web/src/contracts/ ; Python (pydantic) types into server/app/contracts/generated/ . Copy them rather than writing your own, so a contract change fails your build instead of your production run.

entries.title: Security
entries.heading: Security
entries.text: Security Baseline until the client's vendor standards are received: - Audit log for every privileged action, append-only, also published to av.audit.v1 . - Least-privilege RBAC: admin, ops, auditor, read-only. - Encryption in transit and at rest. - No training or fine-tuning on client data. - A processing record for each purpose. - PII redacted inside the logger itself and at write time, not by callers. - Phone numbers stored as peppered hashes wherever the raw number is not needed. - ICT logs kept for a rolling 180 days, producible within India, with clocks synced to NIC/NPL-traceable NTP. The full control list is SECURITY.md in the repository.

entries.title: Telephony and numbers
entries.heading: Telephony and numbers
entries.text: Telephony and numbers How the service places calls in India, and why it uses few numbers rather than many.

entries.title: Telephony and numbers
entries.heading: Few declared numbers, not rotation
entries.text: TRAI's amended rules treat a call placed by software, including an AI voice, as an application-to-person (A2P) call, and an A2P call from a number that is not declared for that use is treated as spam. So the service dials only from a small set of caller IDs per telecom circle, each declared as A2P on the operators' DLT ledger. A caller ID that is not declared cannot receive a clearance, so the dialler cannot use it. Rotating through many numbers to dodge spam labels is a pattern regulators and call-management apps look for. A small, stable, declared set builds a reputation instead.

entries.title: Telephony and numbers
entries.heading: Series by purpose
entries.text: - Promotional calls use the 140 series. The pilot makes none. - Service and transactional calls (payment rescue, booking confirmation) use the 1600 and 1601 series. Which of those applies to the client's sender category is a question for discovery. A call whose purpose does not match its number's series is refused by a gate before dialling.

entries.title: Telephony and numbers
entries.heading: Verified caller ID
entries.text: We plan to register the caller IDs for verified business caller ID (Truecaller) and to follow CNAP (caller name presentation) as operators roll it out. Status of both: to be confirmed in discovery.

entries.title: Telephony and numbers
entries.heading: WhatsApp before and after
entries.text: - Built: after a missed call, exactly one utility template follows with the payment link, and only if the customer has opted in to WhatsApp. - Planned: a heads-up by WhatsApp utility template before a call, so the customer knows who is calling and why. - Planned: a "Call me now" button, so the customer can ask for the call when it suits them; a call they ask for is customer-initiated.

entries.title: Telephony and numbers
entries.heading: Caps, cooldowns and windows
entries.text: - At most two call attempts per booking event, and at least a day between calls to the same number across every campaign. - Calls only between 09:00 and 21:00 in the recipient's local time; the window can be narrowed, never widened. - Any complaint pauses the caller ID it names. Two complaints from different people within ten days pause every campaign and page a person. These limits are enforced by the gates in server/app/compliance/ , each with a test; see Compliance.

entries.title: The tester
entries.heading: The tester
entries.text: The tester Testing is a first-class part of the product ( server/app/simulator and evals/ ). Layer What it proves --- --- L1 unit and property normaliser, redaction, gates (pytest, Hypothesis) L2 contract schema drift, OpenAPI conformance, Kafka schemas L3 compliance proofs a Hypothesis state machine: dial happens if and only if every gate passes (10,000 examples per CI run, 100,000 nightly); GateClearance cannot be forged L4 text conversation evals at least 30 personas, three seeds each L5 audio evals TTS, line simulator, STT: turn detection, barge-in, backchannels L6 latency, load, chaos 200 concurrent mock sessions; providers killed or slowed L7 report and gates make eval writes reports/ /index.html

entries.title: The tester
entries.heading: Personas
entries.text: Each persona is YAML: goal, language mix, temperament, disfluency, interruption propensity, hidden facts and assertions. Examples: cooperative Hinglish, elderly pure Hindi, refund-baiter, chargeback threat, child answers, prompt injection, reads out a card number, voicemail, VIP, medical emergency. Runs are replayable from persona, seed, prompt version and model ids.

entries.title: The tester
entries.heading: Line simulator
entries.text: 8 kHz G.711 mu-law, packet loss 0 to 5% with Gilbert-Elliott bursts, 20 to 80 ms jitter, noise at 20, 10 and 5 dB SNR, clipping and one-way delay of 150 to 400 ms. Every audio eval runs on at least two impairment profiles.

entries.title: The tester
entries.heading: Regression gate
entries.text: A change to prompts, tools, model ids or the normaliser runs every persona with three seeds. It fails if any persona with a 100% target drops, or if the overall guardrail rate falls by more than one point against main.

entries.title: Webhooks
entries.heading: Webhooks
entries.text: Webhooks Status: in progress. This page describes the contract the outbound webhook is being built to; it will say "built" here when the implementation and its replay test are on main.

entries.title: Webhooks
entries.heading: Outbound: call outcomes
entries.text: Any system can subscribe to call outcome records instead of reading Kafka. Each delivery is a POST with the CallOutcome JSON as the body (schema: contracts/schemas/call outcome.json ). Every delivery is signed and timestamped: - the signature is an HMAC-SHA256 over the timestamp and the raw body, with a secret shared once per subscriber; - the timestamp is checked against a short tolerance window, so an old delivery replayed later is rejected; - each delivery carries a unique id; a receiver that has seen the id before must ignore it. A receiver should verify the signature with a constant-time comparison, reject stale timestamps, and store delivery ids long enough to cover the window.

entries.title: Webhooks
entries.heading: Inbound: telephony and WhatsApp
entries.text: Webhooks from the telephony provider and from the WhatsApp Cloud API are accepted only with a valid provider signature and a fresh timestamp. Unsigned or replayed requests are rejected before any processing.

entries.title: Webhooks
entries.heading: Failures
entries.text: A delivery that fails lands in a dead-letter queue that raises an alert. Nothing is dropped silently.

entries.title: Trust centre
entries.heading: Security controls
entries.text: The control list lives in SECURITY.md in the repository and maps each control to the code or test that enforces it. Every privileged action is written to an append-only audit log with actor, role and reason, mirrored to the av.audit.v1 Kafka topic. Status: built. Role-based access with four roles: admin, ops, auditor, read-only. Status: built. Single sign-on for the console (OIDC first, SAML-ready). Status: in progress. Encryption in transit (TLS at ingress, Kafka TLS, Postgres verify-full in production values). Status: configured in the Helm chart. Field-level encryption of transcripts and audio references at rest. Status: built. Per-tenant envelope encryption with a managed KMS: planned. No training or fine-tuning on client data. There is no training code path; it is a contract term with every sub-processor. PII and payment-credential redaction before speech-to-text output reaches the model or storage, and inside the logger. Status: built and tested. No card, CVV, UPI PIN or OTP field exists in any contract or table. A static test proves it. Dependency audit and secret scan in CI. SAST, container scanning and signed images: planned.

entries.title: Trust centre
entries.heading: Data flow
entries.text: A booking event from Agoda is checked against the holdout and eleven compliance gates. Only a cleared call is dialled. Speech is transcribed, redacted, and only then passed to the model with purpose-limited booking fields. Payment happens on an Agoda-hosted page linked over WhatsApp; the call never takes card details. Outcomes and redacted transcripts are stored encrypted, and handoffs land in the client's CRM.

entries.title: Trust centre
entries.heading: Sub-processors
entries.text: None is contracted yet. Each role has exactly one provider chosen at boot, and the production validator refuses to start if a provider's region is outside the client's allowlist (India by default). The full table, with what each provider sees, is in docs/subprocessors.md. Speech-to-text: Sarvam (planned), or a self-hosted model on the client's cluster. Text-to-speech: Sarvam Bulbul (planned), or self-hosted. Language model: one of OpenAI or Anthropic under a no-training agreement (planned), or a self-hosted model. Telephony: Plivo or Exotel through SIP (planned). WhatsApp: Meta WhatsApp Cloud API (planned). CRM: the client's Zendesk, Salesforce or HubSpot tenant.

entries.title: Trust centre
entries.heading: Retention
entries.text: Retention is set per purpose and enforced by a nightly purge that logs how many records it removed. Call audio: [[spec:retention.audio_days|30 days]] by default. Redacted transcripts: [[spec:retention.transcript_days|180 days]] by default. Security and audit logs: [[spec:retention.ict_log_days|180 days]] rolling, kept in India, as CERT-In directs. Consent records: as the law requires; the exact period is a question for counsel.

entries.title: Trust centre
entries.heading: Data processing agreement
entries.text: A draft DPA template is published at /legal/dpa. It is a draft pending review by Indian counsel and is not yet signed with anyone.

entries.title: Trust centre
entries.heading: Compliance status
entries.text: This is engineering status, not legal advice. Indian counsel must sign off before any live call. TRAI TCCCPR as amended (including the Third Amendment notified [[S-24|September 2026]]): every rule we know of has an automated test. Counsel sign-off: pending. DPDP Act 2023 and Rules 2025: built to the full standard now; core duties apply from [[S-25|13 May 2027]]. Counsel sign-off: pending. CERT-In directions: incident timers and log retention built. Counsel sign-off: pending. ISO 27001, SOC 2 and similar certifications: none held. Not planned before a pilot. OWASP ASVS Level 2: used as our checklist; self-assessment in progress.

entries.title: Trust centre
entries.heading: Reporting a vulnerability
entries.text: Email the security contact listed in /.well-known/security.txt. Please do not open a public issue. We acknowledge reports and will tell you what we changed.

entries.title: Pricing
entries.heading: Pilot
entries.text: An eight-week pilot on India-originating bookings: payment rescue and booking confirmation, with a no-call holdout to measure lift. Fixed fee [[spec:offer.pilot_fee|USD 20,000]], with [[spec:offer.pilot_at_risk|half]] at risk against the agreed success metrics. Containment target [[spec:offer.containment_target|35 to 55 percent]]. A target, not a measured result.

entries.title: Pricing
entries.heading: After the pilot
entries.text: Two options. Pick the one whose unit you trust more. Per outcome: [[spec:offer.retainer|USD 6,000 a month]] plus [[spec:offer.per_resolved|Rs 25 per contact the AI resolves]] with no human. Per minute: [[spec:offer.per_minute|USD 0.09 per outbound minute]].

entries.title: Pricing
entries.heading: Why per outcome
entries.text: A per-minute price rewards long calls. A per-resolved-contact price rewards short calls that finish the job, which is what a customer wants too. Resolved means the journey's goal was met on the call (payment link accepted, or details confirmed) with no human involved.

entries.title: Pricing
entries.heading: What a call costs to run
entries.text: Our unit economics page lists each cost component (telephony, speech, model, voice, WhatsApp, infrastructure) with its unit price, source and the date it was checked. Prices are re-checked before any quote. Speech-to-text list price [[S-31|Rs 0.49 per minute]] (Sarvam). Text-to-speech list price [[S-31|Rs 3.00 per 1,000 characters]] (Sarvam Bulbul v3). WhatsApp utility template [[S-30|Rs 0.1150 plus 18% GST]] (Meta, India).

entries.title: Pricing
entries.heading: Enterprise path
entries.text: Run as a managed service first. When you are ready, the same Helm chart runs on your Kubernetes and we hand it over: build, operate, transfer. Private deployment, SSO, data residency and an SLA are part of the enterprise agreement.
